text:
Nina T: tiny design discussion 1: chart axis unit wording + how we surface smoothing/outlier options in the console. quick thoughts?
Evan M: my vote is for compact units on-axis (e.g., `/s`) and expanded copy in hover/tooltips ("Requests per second (req/s)"). keeps axes tidy but remains readable. :+1:
Priya S: agree on compact axis. also want to raise the legend UX: when smoothing is on we currently show two colored chips (raw + smooth) which doubles height. we should make smoothing toggle collapse raw series into a secondary line in legend with smaller type.
Rob C: +1 to collapse. Accessibility: collapsed item should still be in tab order and expose state via aria-expanded and an accessible label like "Raw series hidden, press enter to reveal".
Nina T: what about outlier handling? product wants "reduce noise" mode. two candidate implementations discussed: 1) clip values at a percentile (affects scale), 2) visual de-emphasis (reduce alpha / stroke width) leaving data intact. which aligns with our principles?
Evan M: de-emphasis is safer. clipping can hide real incidents and affect shared impressions of SLA graphs. de-emphasis keeps interactions (hover, search) consistent.
Priya S: UX copy options: "Suppress spikes" (short but vague), "De-emphasize outliers" (explicit), "Spike smoothing" (confusable with smoothing). prefer "De-emphasize outliers" + helper: "Reduce visual prominence of isolated spikes without changing values."
Rob C: microcopy nit: helper should be <80 chars so it fits compact panels. suggestion: "Fade isolated spikes visually; values unchanged."
Nina T: sounds good. We'll label the control: "De-emphasize outliers" with helper "Fade isolated spikes visually; values unchanged." and put it adjacent to the smoothing toggle so users understand the relation.
UXBot: A11Y checklist: 1) Ensure color+alpha isn't the only signal; expose an aria-live region announcing "Outlier de-emphasis enabled" when toggled. 2) Provide text alternative in chart caption when enabled. 3) Ensure contrast of the faded points meets minimum when focused.
Evan M: implementation detail suggestion: don't remove raw series from the DOM; instead apply a CSS class `.chart-point--faded` with lowered opacity and `pointer-events: auto` so hover still works. Also add `aria-hidden=\"false\"` for semantics and an offscreen text node for screen readers describing the state.
Priya S: small code example for the legend collapse styling:
```
.legend-item--collapsed { color: var(--muted-600); font-size: 12px; }
.legend-item--collapsed .toggle { text-decoration: underline; }
.legend-item--collapsed:focus { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); }
```
Make sure focus outline is visible on keyboard and high contrast themes.
Rob C: keyboard flow proposal: `G` to focus graph, `L` to jump to legend, arrow keys to move between items, space/enter to toggle raw series visibility. Document in keyboard shortcuts modal.
Nina T: unit decision: `/s` on axis, legend shows `req/s`, tooltip shows "Requests per second (req/s)" sentence case. Priya, can you update tooltip copy?
Priya S: will do. also propose we add a short hover hint on the axis label that says "Click to toggle full unit" that expands to "requests per second (req/s)" if user wants explicit text on axis.
Evan M: test plan: enable behind feature flag `console.featureFlags.outlierFadeV1`, rollout to internal teams, gather feedback on whether users miss clipping.
Nina T: PR checklist before merge: keyboard focus states, aria-live messages, helper copy under 80 chars, feature flag, unit tooltip text. I'll attach the figma mock momentarily. :mag_right:
UXBot: Reminder: include unit tests for legend keyboard interaction and an accessibility test that asserts the aria-live message is emitted when toggling de-emphasis.
Nina T: thanks all 1. I'll open the PR and tag `#beta-testing` when ready.
